sm: Hosts Patrick Whitlock and Tate Matthews open the Williamson County sports show in the third week of November, noting that wrestling season is starting and the basketball preview will wait until after Thanksgiving break. They go through bowling results, including Page boys going one and one with a high team total of 2,812, Corbin Sanders rolling a 254, and the Centennial boys beating Franklin on a senior night. They then turn to the winter media day, which for the first time included wrestling programs. They preview Greenwood, Fairview, which hopes to qualify fourteen wrestlers for state, and Page, which is young and will host the region tournament.

The wrestling preview continues with Brentwood, which went 24 and 3 in duals but graduated nine starters, Nolensville, led by senior Jake Sentel, Summit with eleven starters back, and Franklin with twelve returning starters including Luke Childs. The hosts say Cleveland remains the team to beat, but Williamson County schools are always close and maybe 2027 is the year. Whitlock then criticizes a Tennessee athletic association proposal that would let school coaches run independent teams in the offseason with no restrictions, calling it Wild West. The vote comes on Thursday the nineteenth. Football recaps begin with Fairview beating Covington 28 to 21, forcing six turnovers to improve to 12 and 0, with quarterback Isaac Burgos throwing two touchdowns.

The hosts discuss Independence-area heartbreak as Kirkwood lost 28 to 27 to Nolensville after erasing a 17 point deficit, with praise for Ryan Newell, Tristan Litham, and Jake Sentel and for Coach Statham's program. Page beat Henry County 28 to 14 to reach its sixth straight Class 5 quarterfinal and moved to 11 and 1. Brentwood fell at Southwind 28 to 20 in the second round of Class 6A, ending a season with only three losses. They say the Bruins have good players returning, including quarterback Gavin String, but lose key linemen and seniors like Parker Emerson and Jones Merrill.

The hosts discuss Ravenwood's 17 to 16 loss to Whitehaven, in which Caden Pace ran for 162 yards. They note that Whitehaven reportedly forfeited three earlier games for using ineligible players, and that a Whitehaven kicker hit a 38 yard field goal for the win. Whitlock suggests there may be an investigation and argues that eligibility violations deserve serious punishment, while praising the state association staff as under-resourced. They talk about the one-time transfer rule and wish for neighborhood schools. They praise Ravenwood's senior class and coach Rodriguez for going for it on fourth down, and say the team has many linemen returning.

The hosts finish with the football picks. Tate leads the season pick contest 56 to 29 after going four and one, while Whitlock is 55 and 30. Both pick Fairview, now 13 and 0, to beat Dyersburg, praising the Yellow Jacket defense and Coach Hughes. For Page against Beech, Whitlock picks Page 28 to 21, while Tate takes Beech plus three and a half points. The show ran under thirty minutes, and the hosts say the basketball preview returns after Thanksgiving. They thank the station staff and viewers, and encourage people to attend the state championship games.
